name: BloomBeans (BBT) unprotected setRegistry enables unlimited mint
summary: BBToken.setRegistry had no access control, and mint() authorised any caller the registry returned for a protocol role. The attacker pointed the token at its own registry naming the caller, minted 1e18 BEAN, and sold it into the BEAN/WETH pair and into the BEAN/BLM pair, dumping the BLM into the BLM/USDC pair.
notes: The proxy was upgraded twice before the exploit; the third implementation, set in 0xf2aa5ceb, is the one the exploit ran, so that upgrade sets the age even if earlier implementations shared the bug. The registry pointer the attacker overwrote had been set by the deployer at launch and was unchanged until the anchor; the only mints before it were the initial supply.

Victims are the BEAN/WETH, BEAN/BLM and BLM/USDC pairs netted together, so the BLM taken from the BEAN/BLM pair and dumped into the BLM/USDC pair counts once, as that pair's USDC. The copycat 0x167775a4, the next transaction in the block from another sender, repeated the mint against already-drained pools and took dust.
